title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 37-38
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 37 to 38 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अशोकस्तारणस्तारः शूरः शौरिर्जनेश्वरः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 37 to 38 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 37 to 38.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 37 to 38** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अशोकस्तारणस्तारः शूरः शौरिर्जनेश्वरः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अशोकस्तारणस्तारः शूरः शौरिर्जनेश्वरः । अनुकूलः शतावर्तः पद्मी पद्मनिभेक्षणः ॥** **पद्मनाभोऽरविन्दाक्षः पद्मगर्भः शरीरभृत् । महर्द्धिर्ऋद्धो वृद्धात्मा महाक्षो गरुडध्वजः ॥**

He is free of sorrow, the one who carries us across and protects. The brave one, Shauri, lord of the people, is that God of gods. Ever kind, returning in hundreds of forms, lotus in hand, with eyes like the lotus. A lotus navel, lotus eyes, dwelling in the lotus of the heart is he. The one who supports every body is that God of gods. Of great wealth, vast eyes and the Garuda banner is he.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 37 to 38 mean?
faq.a: He is free of sorrow, the one who carries us across and protects. The brave one, Shauri, lord of the people, is that God of gods. Ever kind, returning in hundreds of forms, lotus in hand, with eyes like the lotus. A lotus navel, lotus eyes, dwelling in the lotus of the heart is he. The one who supports every body is that God of gods. Of great wealth, vast eyes and the Garuda banner is he.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
